title: Ephemeral log trimmer and priority snapshot orchestrator
author: Maya Fernandez
description: Problem: On high-noise incidents the incident-bot snapshot payload grows quickly and responders report slow load times when attaching full telemetry archives. Motivation: reduce on-call cognitive load and bandwidth by trimming ephemeral verbose logs while guaranteeing that high-priority traces and metric snapshots remain fast to retrieve. This PR implements two coordinated features: (1) an ephemeral log trimmer that runs as a post-capture step to collapse repetitive lines, redact high-frequency debug noise, and index retained spans by priority tags; (2) a priority snapshot orchestrator that precomputes compact telemetry bundles for the on-call UI during configured "quiet windows" (low alert volume) so responders get near-instant access to hot traces and metric rollups even for large systems. Implementation highlights: - New capture pipeline hook in incident-capture: capture/hooks/ephemeral_trim.go that performs lossy-preserving trimming with configurable heuristics (dedupe runs, frequency thresholds, pattern clusters). - Priority index: capture/meta/priority_index.go adds lightweight indices (top span ids, top-err patterns, metric rollups) serialized alongside the snapshot. - Orchestrator service: srv/snapshot_orchestrator.go implements a scheduler that detects quiet windows via SLO-backed alert-rate signals and enqueues prefetch tasks to the cache tier. - Config and safety: operator-config.yaml entries with safe defaults (max_trim_ratio, preserve_patterns) and a dry-run flag used in tests. - Backwards compat: trimmed snapshots include a metadata flag so older clients ignore the index and fallback to full download. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for trimming logic and pattern clustering (capture/hooks/ephemeral_trim_test.go). - Integration test that runs a simulated alert flood and verifies prefetch runs during low-rate windows (tests/integration/prefetch_quiet_window_test.go). - Load test: local perf harness shows 35-45% reduction in snapshot payload size for high-noise captures and median UI load time improvement from 1.6s to 0.7s in the Canary harness. Rollout plan: feature gated behind incident-bot.experimental.ephemeral_trimmer and experimental.priority_prefetch flags. Default: off for managed customers; opt-in for internal SRE and canary tenants. Linear links: ENG-4281 (ephemeral capture optimizations), SRE-102 (on-call latency improvements).

release_notes:
- Introduce ephemeral log trimming to reduce snapshot payloads in high-noise incidents (opt-in behind feature flag)
- Add priority snapshot orchestrator to precompute compact telemetry bundles during quiet windows to improve on-call UI load times
- Operator-tunable heuristics and safety defaults; PII redaction regressions covered by tests
impact_and_rollout: Low-risk feature-gated rollout. Initial canary on SRE tenant + internal staging; operator must confirm behavior before enabling for managed customers. Trim defaults conservative to avoid information loss.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-4320: Dashboard for trimmed-volume per-tenant and UI indicator for trimmed chunks
ENG-4331: Expose 'prefetch success/failure' metrics and backoff tuning
